patient_persona.description: Encik Rosli bin Kassim, 42, male, production supervisor at a factory in Shah Alam; neighbour had dengue last month. Medium-pitched, tired, speaks slowly with a sore head.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Lim Wei Jie, Malaysian Chinese man in his 30s, GP at a Shah Alam clinic. Brisk but kind; English-leaning, speaks simple Malay to Malay patients.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Encik Rosli, silakan duduk. Demam dah berapa hari?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Empat hari dah, doktor. Mula hari Ahad malam, demam tinggi, kepala sakit sangat dekat belakang mata.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Badan sakit-sakit? Sendi, tulang?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ya, macam tulang nak patah. Semalam saya ada makan ubat tahan sakit, yang Ponstan tu, isteri saya punya.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: OK, Ponstan tu mefenamic acid. Kalau dengue, ubat macam tu boleh buat berdarah. Mulai hari ni, stop Ponstan, stop ibuprofen, makan Panadol saja.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Oh, tak tahu pula. Jiran sebelah rumah saya bulan lepas kena denggi, masuk hospital Shah Alam.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ada muntah? Sakit perut? Gusi berdarah atau hidung berdarah?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Muntah tak ada. Loya sikit je. Gusi tak berdarah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Temperature 38.6, blood pressure 118 over 76. Saya dah buat NS1 test tadi, positive. Maksudnya encik memang ada denggi.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Teruk ke doktor? Kena masuk wad ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Platelet 142, masih OK. Hematocrit pun normal. Hari ni boleh balik, tapi hari ketiga sampai ketujuh ni masa paling bahaya.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Minum air banyak, sekurang-kurangnya dua setengah liter sehari. Air kosong, jus, air isotonik. Panadol 1 gram, empat kali sehari, maksimum.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Air 100 Plus boleh ke doktor? Saya memang tak suka minum air kosong.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Boleh. Esok pagi datang balik, kita check FBC setiap hari sampai demam hilang dua hari. Saya bagi MC tiga hari dulu.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kalau jadi teruk malam ni, macam mana?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kalau sakit perut kuat, muntah berulang, berdarah, atau rasa nak pitam, terus pergi emergency. Jangan tunggu esok.

patient_persona.description: Ooi Hui Min, 28, female, accounts executive in Bayan Lepas, Penang; lives in a condo where fogging was done last week. Soft voice, anxious, Penang Mandarin with some Hokkien-flavoured words.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Nurul Huda binti Azmi, Malay woman in her 30s, medical officer at a Penang government health clinic. Warm, methodical; English-leaning, speaks functional Mandarin mixed with English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hui Min，你今天是 day 5 了对吗？昨天 platelet 是 98。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 对，医生。昨天晚上烧退了，我以为好了，可是今天早上开始肚子很痛。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 痛在哪里？指给我看。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 这边，右边上面。然后我 vomit 了三次，喝水也吐。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hmm, right upper abdominal pain, persistent vomiting. 这两个是 warning signs。你刷牙的时候牙肉有没有流血？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 有一点点。还有腿上有很多小红点。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 我看看。嗯，这个是 petechiae。今天的 blood test 出来了，platelet 剩下 41，hematocrit 从 38 升到 45。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 这样是不是很严重？我妈妈说要喝木瓜叶汁，platelet 就会上来。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 木瓜叶汁没有证据可以救你。现在最重要的是 fluid。Hematocrit 升高表示血管在漏水，你需要 admit 去 Hospital Pulau Pinang。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 一定要住院吗？我明天还有 audit meeting。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 一定要。这个是 critical phase，可以在几个钟头里面变 shock。我给你开 MC，工作的事情可以等。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好吧……那我可以自己 drive 去吗？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 不可以。我们用 ambulance 送你，现在先打 drip，normal saline。你家里有人可以来吗？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我打给我男朋友，他在 Gelugor 上班，二十分钟就到。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 好。在医院他们会每几个钟头验血，看你的 urine output。不要吃 Ponstan 或者 Voltaren，只能吃 Panadol。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 明白了。谢谢你，医生，我刚才真的很怕。

patient_persona.description: Mr. Selvaraj a/l Pillai, 55, male, lorry transport business owner in Seremban; type 2 diabetes on metformin. Gravelly voice, weak, Malaysian Indian English with Malay words.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Farah Liyana binti Ahmad, Malay woman in her 30s, medical registrar on the morning ward round at Hospital Tuanku Ja'afar Seremban. Crisp, reassuring; English with some Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good morning, Mr. Selvaraj. I'm Dr. Farah from the medical team. How are you feeling today, compared to last night?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Morning, doctor. Last night very bad, I felt like fainting when I went to the toilet. Now a bit better but badan lemah sangat lah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, the nurses told me your blood pressure dropped to 86 over 60 around midnight. That's why we gave you the fluid bolus.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Is that the dengue shock thing? My son read on Google and got very takut.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: It was early shock, compensated. We caught it early. This morning BP is 112 over 74, pulse 96, and your urine output is back above 0.5 ml per kg.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, platelet how much now? Semalam they said very low.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Platelet is 18 today. But hematocrit came down from 49 to 42, which is good. It means the leakage is slowing.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Eighteen only? Don't need to give me platelet, ah? My sepupu last time got transfusion.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Not unless you are bleeding badly. Platelets usually go up on their own once you're past this phase. Any black stools, or muntah darah?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No, stool normal colour. Only the gums a bit berdarah when I brush.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: OK, use a soft brush. Your sugar was 14 this morning, so we're holding metformin and giving insulin while you're on drip.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Insulin? After this I must take insulin selama-lamanya or what?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: No, this is temporary. Infection and the drip make the sugar high. Once you're eating properly we go back to metformin 1 gram twice a day.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: When can I go home, doctor? My business, nobody is handling. Susah lah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Honestly, hari ni belum boleh. We need you stable with no fever, platelets rising, and eating well for at least a day. Maybe two or three days.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Aiyo. OK lah, better safe. Thank you, doctor.

patient_persona.description: Puan Wan Norazila binti Wan Ismail, 36, female, primary school teacher in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, speaking for her son Aiman, 9. Kelantanese Malay accent, quick, worried.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Tengku Hafiz, Malay man in his 40s, paediatrician at a Kota Bharu private hospital. Patient, gentle; switches easily to Kelantan-friendly Malay with English medical terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Assalamualaikum, puan. Keputusan darah Aiman semalam dah keluar. NS1 positif, jadi memang denggi.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ya Allah. Doktor, dia demam dah tiga hari, tapi pagi ni dia nak makan roti sikit.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Bagus tu. Platelet dia 165, hematocrit 37. Hari ni masih normal. Dia kencing macam biasa?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kencing ada, pagi tadi sekali, tengah hari sekali. Warna kuning sikit.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: OK. Saya nak puan catat berapa kali dia kencing, dan berapa banyak dia minum. Sasaran untuk berat dia, lebih kurang 1.5 liter sehari.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doktor, mak mertua saya suruh bagi jus daun betik. Boleh ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Jus daun betik tu tak terbukti bantu, dan pahit, boleh buat budak muntah. Lebih baik air, susu, air sup, jus buah.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ubat demam dia saya bagi Uphamol syrup. Betul ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Betul. Uphamol 250mg per 5ml, dia 28 kilo, bagi 8ml, setiap enam jam kalau demam. Jangan bagi Nurofen.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Lapan ml, enam jam sekali. Baik. Dia boleh pergi sekolah esok?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tak boleh. Rehat di rumah dulu. Hari keempat sampai ketujuh ni kita kena pantau betul-betul. Esok datang ambil darah lagi.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tanda bahaya apa yang saya kena tengok, doktor?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Sakit perut, muntah banyak kali, lemau sangat, tangan kaki sejuk, atau tak kencing lebih enam jam. Kalau ada, terus bawa ke emergency.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Adik dia pun batuk sikit semalam. Takut kena juga.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Denggi tak berjangkit terus antara orang, dia melalui nyamuk Aedes. Cuma kena buang air bertakung sekeliling rumah, dan pasang ubat nyamuk.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Baik doktor, nanti suami saya cuci pasu bunga tu semua. Terima kasih.

patient_persona.description: Juliana Lajim, 35, female, Kadazan hotel front-desk supervisor in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah; discharged from hospital four days ago. Bright voice, chatty, Sabahan English mixed with Malay and the particle 'bah'.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Chong Mei Fong, Sabahan Chinese woman in her 40s, family physician at a Kota Kinabalu clinic. Relaxed, practical; English with Sabahan Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hi Juliana, you look much better than the discharge letter sounds. How's the energy?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Better, doctor, but still penat bah. I climb stairs at home, halfway already need to rest.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: That's normal after dengue. Fatigue can last two to three weeks. Anything else bothering you?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ya, ruam ni. Since two days, my legs and hands so itchy, especially at night. Red with small white spots.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me see. Ah, this is the typical convalescent rash, what we call isles of white in a sea of red. It's a sign of recovery.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Oh really? I thought allergic to the ubat from hospital.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Unlikely. It usually fades in a week. For the itch, calamine lotion, and cetirizine 10mg at night if you can't sleep.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: OK. Doctor, today's result darah macam mana?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Platelet 210, back to normal. Liver enzyme ALT is 96, still a bit high, but coming down from 180.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Liver high? Must stop anything? I take Panadol sometimes for sakit kepala.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Keep Panadol to maximum 2 grams a day for now, and no alcohol for a few weeks. We repeat the liver test in two weeks.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No problem, I don't drink also. When can I work? Front desk, berdiri whole day.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I'll give you MC until Sunday. Start Monday, maybe ask your manager for half-day the first few days.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: OK bah. And can I get dengue again? My kampung in Penampang, so many mosquito.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, there are four types, and a second infection can be more severe. So repellent, buang air bertakung, and see a doctor early next time.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Aiyo, scary. OK doctor, I'll tell my keluarga also. Thank you.

patient_persona.description: Encik Juanis bin Gidong, 50, male, oil palm smallholder near Keningau, Sabah; often works at the forest edge. Deep voice, slow, Sabahan Malay with 'bah' and 'sia'.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Ahmad Syazwan, Malay man in his 30s, medical officer doing the morning ward round at Hospital Keningau. Friendly; English-leaning, speaks Malay with patients.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Selamat pagi, Encik Juanis. Macam mana rasa pagi ni? Masih menggigil?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Pagi, doktor. Sudah kurang bah. Semalam menggigil teruk, sekarang cuma lemah sikit.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Baik. Blood film semalam tunjuk Plasmodium knowlesi, yang malaria monyet tu. Parasite count 12,000.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Malaria monyet? Memang banyak monyet ekor panjang dekat kebun sawit saya.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ya, nyamuk gigit monyet, lepas tu gigit encik. Knowlesi ni boleh naik cepat, sebab tu kita bagi IV artesunate semalam.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ubat drip itu? Berapa kali lagi mesti cucuk?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tiga dos IV dah cukup. Hari ni kalau encik boleh makan, kita tukar ke tablet Riamet, artemether-lumefantrine, tiga hari.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tablet itu macam mana makan?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Empat biji setiap kali, dua kali sehari, tiga hari. Kena makan dengan makanan berlemak sikit, macam susu atau roti mentega, supaya ubat masuk badan.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Oh, mesti makan dengan susu. OK. Doktor, darah saya macam mana? Kata platelet rendah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Platelet 64, rendah, memang biasa dengan knowlesi. Buah pinggang pun kita check, creatinine 98, normal.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Isteri saya dan anak di rumah, boleh kena juga ka dari saya?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tak berjangkit terus dari orang ke orang. Tapi pejabat kesihatan akan datang buat semburan dan check orang lain di kampung.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Bila saya boleh balik rumah, doktor? Sawit sudah boleh potong minggu ni.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mungkin lusa, kalau blood film negatif dan platelet naik. Lepas balik, pakai lengan panjang dan ubat nyamuk kalau ke kebun waktu senja.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Baik doktor. Terima kasih banyak bah.

condition: Falciparum malaria in a returning traveller

patient_persona.description: Mr. Daniel Anyi, 38, male, Iban offshore drilling engineer from Miri, Sarawak, back from a six-week rotation in Nigeria. Mid-pitched, articulate, mostly English with a little Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Rachel Tiong, Sarawakian Chinese woman in her 30s, emergency physician at Hospital Miri. Focused, fast; English with Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mr. Daniel, the triage note says fever and chills for three days. When did you come back from overseas?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ten days ago, from Port Harcourt, Nigeria. Six-week rotation on the rig. Fever started Tuesday, then shivering every few hours.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Did you take any malaria prophylaxis, like Malarone or doxycycline?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: The company gave doxycycline 100mg. I took it on the rig, but I stopped once I landed. Nobody told me to continue.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Doxycycline must be continued for four weeks after leaving. That's a common mistake. Any headache, confusion, dark urine?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Headache yes, sakit sangat. Urine a bit dark this morning. Confusion, I don't think so.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Temperature 39.4, pulse 118, BP 104 over 68. The rapid test is positive for falciparum. We're sending thick and thin films now.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Falciparum is the dangerous one, right? My colleague got it two years ago.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: It can be, so we treat it seriously. You'll be admitted, and we start IV artesunate 2.4mg per kg straight away.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Terus masuk wad? OK. How long usually?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: At least three to four days, until the parasite count clears and you can take tablets. Then a full oral course to finish.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: My wife is pregnant, lima bulan. Is she at risk from me?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: No, malaria doesn't spread person to person here. But if she travels with you in future, she must see us first, pregnancy and malaria is serious.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Faham, doctor. I'm supposed to fly back to Nigeria in four weeks.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: We'll talk about proper prophylaxis before you go. And if you get fever within three months of travel, always say you went to Africa, terus.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Noted, doctor. I'll call my wife to bring my baju.

patient_persona.description: Wong Chee Keong, 33, male, Foochow construction foreman from Sibu, Sarawak, recently back from a project in Papua New Guinea. Loud, direct, Mandarin with Sibu inflection and English work words.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Ling Siew Hua, Foochow woman in her 40s, physician at Hospital Sibu medical clinic. Calm, thorough; Mandarin with English medical terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 黄先生，你出院两个礼拜了，今天是 follow-up。现在感觉怎样？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好很多了，医生。不发烧了，胃口也回来了，就是还有一点累。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 正常的。今天的 blood film 我看了，已经没有 parasite 了。Haemoglobin 是 11.2，比出院的时候高。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那就好。住院的时候他们说我的 parasite 很多，吓死我。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 对，入院的时候是百分之四，算 severe。还好你那天就来了，没有拖。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 其实我在 PNG 已经发烧一次，以为是 flu，吃 Panadol 就好了。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 那次很可能也是 malaria。以后去那种地方，要吃 prophylaxis。你们公司有安排吗？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 没有，是小公司。我下个月又要去 Lae 那边做工，三个月。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 那我建议你吃 Malarone，atovaquone-proguanil，出发前一天开始，每天一粒，回来以后再吃七天。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 每天一粒，回来还要吃七天。贵不贵？一粒多少 ringgit？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 比较贵，一粒大概十几块。另一个选择是 doxycycline 100mg，便宜很多，可是回来后要吃四个礼拜，还要防晒。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我在外面晒太阳做工，那还是 Malarone 好了。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 好。还有，住的地方要有蚊帐，晚上穿长袖，用 DEET 的驱蚊水。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我的 workers 也要吃吗？他们都是本地人。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 本地人也会得，只是比较常见。他们应该看当地的医生。你自己回来以后三个月内发烧，马上来验血。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 明白了。谢谢医生，这次真的学到了。

patient_persona.description: Koperal Mohd Hafizi bin Zulkifli, 26, male, army corporal from Pasir Mas, Kelantan, back from jungle operations near the Kelantan-Perak border. Polite, crisp, Kelantanese Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Siti Aminah binti Yusof, Malay woman in her 40s, family medicine specialist at a Kota Bharu health clinic. Direct, motherly; Malay with English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hafizi, hari ni hari ke-28 lepas rawatan. Kita buat blood film terakhir. Ada demam balik tak sejak keluar wad?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tak ada, doktor. Saya dah sihat. Dah mula lari pagi dengan unit saya minggu lepas.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Jangan paksa sangat dulu. Hemoglobin masa discharge 10.8. Hari ni kita check sekali lagi.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Baik doktor. Kawan saya satu platun pun kena malaria, tapi dia dekat Hospital Gua Musang.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ya, pejabat kesihatan dah maklumkan. Operasi dekat hutan tu, kawasan knowlesi. Dia orang dah buat screening semua anggota.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doktor, masa operasi kami ada ubat nyamuk, tapi tak cukup. Malam dalam hutan memang banyak nyamuk.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Knowlesi ni nyamuk dia gigit waktu senja dan awal malam. Lengan panjang, seluar panjang, repellent dengan DEET, dan kelambu yang ada racun.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kelambu tu kami ada, tapi kadang tak sempat pasang.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Saya faham, operasi. Saya akan tulis surat kepada pegawai perubatan unit awak, minta bekalan repellent yang cukup.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Terima kasih doktor. Result hari ni bila keluar?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Dah keluar pun. Blood film negatif, tiada parasit. Hemoglobin naik ke 13.1. Awak dah sembuh sepenuhnya.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Alhamdulillah. Jadi saya boleh masuk operasi balik bulan depan?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Dari segi malaria, boleh. Tapi kalau demam dalam masa setahun lepas masuk hutan, beritahu doktor terus pasal hutan tu.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kalau saya dah pernah kena, badan saya ada imun ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tak. Boleh kena lagi, dan kali kedua pun boleh teruk. Jadi jangan ambil mudah.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Faham, doktor. Saya akan pesan dekat kawan-kawan juga.

condition: Fever in a returning traveller, malaria excluded

patient_persona.description: Priya a/p Ramachandran, 30, female, NGO programme officer in Petaling Jaya, back from three weeks volunteering in Uganda. Clear, fast Malaysian Indian English, organised, a bit anxious.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Hazwan bin Rahim, Malay man in his 40s, infectious diseases physician at a PJ private hospital. Measured, precise; English with occasional Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Priya, I have your results. Three sets of malaria films, taken twelve hours apart, all negative. And the rapid antigen test also negative.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Oh thank God. I was so sure it was malaria. My demam was 39 for two days.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Three negative films makes malaria very unlikely. Your dengue NS1 is also negative. But your full blood count shows something else.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Something else? Apa dia, doctor?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: White count is normal, but eosinophils are raised. And you mentioned swimming in Lake Bunyonyi, right?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, on my last weekend. The guide said it's safe, no bilharzia.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Many freshwater lakes in that region carry schistosomiasis. Fever with high eosinophils a few weeks after swimming, that's suspicious.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: So what do we do now?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: We'll send schistosoma serology, and a stool and urine test for eggs. Serology might take a week.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And sementara tu? I have a report due next Friday.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: You're stable, so you can go home. Paracetamol 1 gram up to four times a day for fever. If the tests confirm it, the treatment is praziquantel, usually a one-day course.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: One day only? Tak teruk sangat lah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, but we time it right, because it works best on mature worms, so sometimes we repeat it after six to eight weeks.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, I stopped my doxycycline after one week back. Should I start balik?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: It's now past the four weeks, so no need. But if fever comes back in the next three months, come straight here and remind them about Uganda.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: OK, I'll simpan your card. Thank you, doctor.
